chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the amulet that is hung upon the menstruating woman, so he said: 'Yes, if it is inside a skin, or silver, or an iron tube.'

key_terms.التَّعْوِيذ: Amulet or charm containing Quranic verses or prayers

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to hang an amulet on a menstruating woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the permissibility of *ta'widh* (amulets) for menstruating women, a topic of nuance due to their state of major ritual impurity (*hadath akbar*). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that validity is maintained if the text is protected within a barrier like leather, silver, or iron, thereby preventing direct contact with the impurity while allowing the spiritual benefit of the Quranic recitation. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly distinction between the Quran itself being impure versus the person being impure, emphasizing protection rather than prohibition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the amulet hanging upon the menstruating woman. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, when it was (enveloped) inside a skin, or silver, or an iron tube’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of al-Ta‘widh (protective talisman) which women hang on themselves. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, they can do so if it is incased with leather, silver, tube or iron.’”
